This article provides a selected bibliography of research relevant to the definition and analysis of repeated treatment episodes. The literature is organized around two areas: approaches to defining distinct episodes of care and statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal psychotherapy outcomes.

# Studies Using 90-days to demarcate episodes

Several studies have operationalized a new episode of behavioral health care following at least 90 days without treatment [citations]. This definition provides a clinically interpretable rule for distinguishing short interruptions in ongoing treatment from subsequent reengagement.
